questions.question: An EMT team is performing CPR and using an AED while a paramedic prepares IV medication. Which distinction explains these roles?

choices.text: CPR and AED use provide basic support; IV medication is an advanced intervention
AED use is advanced care because it analyzes the rhythm, while IV medication is basic care
Both CPR and IV medication are basic care if neither uses an advanced airway
All three interventions are advanced care because the patient is in cardiac arrest

questions.explanation: BLS supports circulation and ventilation through basic interventions; IV medication is among the described ALS procedures. Provider arrival does not change an intervention’s category.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: Automated defibrillation is included among the chapter’s BLS interventions; IV medications are ALS.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: An IV medication is an advanced intervention even without an advanced airway.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: The arrest diagnosis does not classify all care as ALS.

questions.question: A pulseless adult is on a safe scene. ALS is arriving in several minutes, and the AED is being brought to you. What should you do now?

choices.text: Begin high-quality CPR while the AED and ALS are brought into the resuscitation
Finish collecting the medication history before starting CPR
Delay compressions until a monitor identifies the exact rhythm
Wait to begin all care when the paramedic can establish an IV

questions.explanation: CPR must begin rapidly after arrest is recognized; it supports vital-organ perfusion while definitive interventions are arranged.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: Medication history may help subsequent care but cannot take priority over immediate circulation support.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Rhythm identification must not postpone initial compressions.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: IV access does not replace immediate BLS.

questions.question: An adult is unresponsive but has a definite carotid pulse and adequate normal breathing. Which conclusion is supported?

choices.text: The patient needs continued assessment and airway protection, but not chest compressions
Unresponsiveness alone establishes cardiac arrest and requires compressions
The pulse can be disregarded because the patient cannot answer questions
Adequate breathing proves that the patient needs no emergency evaluation

questions.explanation: An unresponsive patient may or may not need CPR. A definite pulse with adequate breathing calls for assessment and appropriate airway protection rather than compressions.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: Unresponsiveness must be considered with breathing and circulation findings.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: A definite pulse is important to the treatment decision.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: Unresponsiveness remains an emergency even when breathing and circulation are present.

questions.question: Why does an adult still require definitive treatment even when CPR is producing effective chest rise and compressions?

choices.text: CPR temporarily supports circulation and ventilation while the cause of arrest and need for defibrillation are addressed
A complete cycle of effective CPR establishes that a shock is no longer needed
Chest rise during rescue breaths confirms that the heart is pumping again
Restoration of external blood flow corrects the underlying cause of every arrest

questions.explanation: CPR buys time by supporting circulation and ventilation; it does not by itself resolve every cause of arrest or replace definitive care.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: CPR effectiveness does not determine that defibrillation is unnecessary; rhythm assessment still matters.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Assisted chest rise demonstrates ventilation, not independent circulation.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: External circulation support does not resolve every underlying cause.

questions.topic: Chain of survival as a system
questions.question: Bystanders activate EMS promptly, but no CPR is performed during the wait for the AED. Why is rapid activation alone insufficient?

choices.text: The chain also requires immediate circulation support while defibrillation and further care are arranged
Early EMS activation replaces bystander CPR when an AED will arrive soon
The AED supports blood flow during the time before pads are attached
Rapid advanced airway placement makes the interval without compressions unimportant

questions.explanation: The links work together. Immediate high-quality CPR supports perfusion during the interval before defibrillation and advanced care.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: An AED has no circulation-support effect while it is being brought to the patient.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: An airway does not compensate for the lack of circulation.

choices.text: Provide ongoing assessment and appropriate oxygenation, monitoring, and advanced post-arrest care

Continue the arrest compression cycle until hospital arrival despite confirmed adequate circulation

questions.question: During cardiac arrest, what is the immediate physiologic purpose of rhythmic chest compressions?

choices.text: To create blood flow to vital organs despite the lack of an effective spontaneous heartbeat
To move fresh oxygen into the lungs in place of rescue breaths
To establish an electrical rhythm that proves the need for a shock

incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: A compression-generated flow does not determine the electrical rhythm or shock indication.
